intro.heading: The matchup
intro.body:
The season comes down to Thursday night. **Klein Cain (5-3, 3-3)** hosts **Magnolia (4-4, 4-2)** on Thursday, October 29 at 7:00 PM at Klein Memorial Stadium, and the math is plain: Cain sits **sixth** in **District 15-6A**, one game behind a four-team tie at 4-2, and Magnolia is one of those four teams. Win, and Cain pulls even with the Bulldogs and takes the **head-to-head edge**. Lose, and the playoff chase ends with a week to spare.

Cain earned this shot on Friday night at Tomball Memorial. **Israel Smith (#8)** scored on a **75-yard** end around on the first play from scrimmage, the defense forced **four turnovers**, and Cain led **37-0** at halftime on the way to a **44-10** win that snapped a three-game skid. **Eyan Johnson (#16)** ran for two touchdowns, including an **80-yard** score in the third quarter, and **Jace Hanks (#9)** threw touchdown passes to **Hank Aguirre (#13)** and **Cooper Karns (#10)**.

Magnolia arrives just as hot. The Bulldogs have won **three straight**, capped by a **48-20** win over Klein Forest on Friday where they led **35-0** after one quarter and rested their starters early. Senior quarterback **Chase Lowery** drives everything: he ran for two touchdowns and threw a 39-yard touchdown pass against Forest, and through the bye week he had **12 rushing touchdowns** with **763 rushing yards** and **1,060 passing yards**. Senior back **Cash Ferrell** added a rushing score against Forest after entering the night with a rushing touchdown in **six straight games**.

The rest of Friday shook the table up. Klein Oak edged Tomball **42-41**, so Klein (6-1) stands alone at the top and Klein Oak, Magnolia, Klein Collins and Tomball are all tied at **4-2**, fighting for the other three playoff spots. Only the **top four** advance. Cain closes at Klein Forest on November 6, and if Cain gets in, it goes **Division I**: at **3,784** students Cain is the largest school in the district, and the two qualifiers with the largest enrollments play in Division I while the other two play in Division II, each division chasing its own state title. Neither team appeared in the **October 19** Class 6A state poll from Dave Campbell's Texas Football. *Thursday night decides whether the chase lives to the final week.*
